paper.authors_full: Xuekang Wu, Guy Aridor, Artem Timoshenko
paper.title: Guided Creativity: AI Intermediation for Enhancing Originality and Quality in Visual Design
paper.venue: Working paper (SSRN 5371575; revision posted on author website)
paper.version_read: Working paper dated March 2, 2026, by Xuekang Wu, Guy Aridor, and Artem Timoshenko; date on the document and Web Appendix title pages.
paper.one_line_finding: In the main logo contest (292 analyzed designers), AI variations increased mean click-attractiveness quality versus Blind (beta_Var - beta_Blind = 0.0665, SE 0.0197) and top-50 submission originality versus human exemplars (beta_Open - beta_Var = -0.0139, SE 0.0053), with no clear quality difference versus human exemplars or originality difference versus Blind, and the restaurant replication (208 analyzed) showed the same direction pattern (PDF pp. 20 and 29, Tables 1-2; PDF p. 64, Tables WA-C.3/WA-C.4; PDF pp. 68-69, Tables WA-D.4/WA-D.5).

sources.locator: PDF p. 36 (printed p. 35), Appendix B, pooled submission depth

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports 575 treatment submissions and 575 control submissions. These are output totals, not people or arm means. No two-arm participant total is printed, so n_total is null; n_units is not used for this participant-level outcome. Appendix B prints only a pooled mean of 7.5 designs and says pairwise t-tests found no statistically significant differences across conditions. It gives no arm means, SDs, t values, degrees of freedom, or exact/bounded p-values. The test object identifies the stated test only; no numerical inference is supplied, so se_basis is not_reported. All pairwise comparisons involving an AI arm are retained, including the two Variation(4)-versus-control comparisons covered by the all-condition statement. Counts are people who submitted, not registrations or numbers of logos. AI exemplars remained available while outputs were produced; this is immediate with_ai, with outcome_with_ai=true and within_person=null. Fluency counts submitted designs; distinct ideas are not established.
estimates.primary_override_reason: Rule 1: The paper explicitly names Variation(1) versus Open and Blind as the main analysis and introduces Variation(4) to compare the number of variations. This makes Variation(1) versus Blind the preferred contrast among the tied submission-depth records. (PDF p. 18 (printed p. 17), Section 4.1, Study Design, paragraph beginning "In this experiment".: "To understand the effectiveness of AI Intermediation, our following main analysis is on the comparison between the Variation(1) and two control conditions.")

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Embedding-based originality; Variation(1) versus Open/Blind and Variation(4) versus Variation(1), including every high-quality-subset specification
not_extracted.reason: Excluded by extraction-spec rule 5. Specification (1) controls for submission date: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 22) states that Dayi controls for the submission date; randomization occurs at registration (PDF p. 19, printed p. 18), so submission date is measured after assignment. The originality regressions additionally select outputs using post-treatment quality: top 50 or 100 per condition, or top 200 or 400 across conditions. See PDF pp. 23-24 and 27 (printed pp. 22-23 and 26), Figures 6 and 9A, and PDF pp. 63-64 (printed WA-19 to WA-20), Tables WA-C.2 and WA-C.4. No full-sample unadjusted originality contrast is printed.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Click-attractiveness quality; all reported mean and quantile contrasts, including Variation(4) versus Variation(1)
not_extracted.reason: All reported specifications adjust for post-assignment submission date. Section 4.4 explicitly reuses Equation (1) (PDF p. 24, printed p. 23); Table WA-C.1 prints a SubmissionTime regressor in every mean/quantile column (PDF p. 62, printed WA-18). Exclusion covers the mean and quantiles at tau = 0.95, 0.90, 0.75, and 0.50, Table WA-C.3 (PDF p. 64, printed WA-20), and Figures 7-9 (PDF pp. 25 and 27, printed pp. 24 and 26). These adjusted condition coefficients are not unadjusted arm means. Figure-only bar heights and interval endpoints are not digitized.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Perception-based originality; Variation versus Open and Blind
not_extracted.reason: Figure C.1 explicitly uses specification (1), which adjusts for post-assignment submission date. See PDF pp. 37-39 (printed pp. 36-38), Appendix C, and PDF p. 23 (printed p. 22), Equation (1). The number and membership of rated submissions/designers are also not stated. Printed text contrasts are excluded rather than treated as unadjusted effects; unlabeled bar heights are not recorded.

not_extracted.what: S2-O1: Embedding-based originality; all Variation-versus-Open/Blind contrasts and robustness subsets
not_extracted.reason: The estimates reuse specification (1) and Table WA-D.2 includes SubmissionTime in every column; it is measured after assignment. Outcomes also use only high-quality subsets, defined by top 50/100 per condition or top 200/400 overall. See PDF p. 30 (printed p. 29), Figure 11A, PDF p. 67 (printed WA-23), Table WA-D.2, and PDF p. 68 (printed WA-24), Table WA-D.4. No full-sample unadjusted originality estimate is printed.

not_extracted.what: S2-O2: Click-attractiveness quality; all Variation-versus-Open/Blind mean and quantile contrasts
not_extracted.reason: Table WA-D.3 adjusts every quality specification for post-assignment SubmissionTime (PDF p. 68, printed WA-24). Exclusion covers the mean and quantiles at tau = 0.95, 0.90, 0.75, and 0.50, Table WA-D.5 and Figure WA-D.2 (PDF p. 69, printed WA-25), and Figure 11B (PDF p. 30, printed p. 29). No unadjusted quality arm means or treatment effects are printed. Figure-only values are not digitized.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: Alignment scores restricted to Top 200, Top 100, and Top 50 submissions per condition
not_extracted.reason: These are post-treatment quality-selected subsets, not full-sample contrasts. PDF p. 44 (printed p. 43), Table E.3 and notes, defines Top X as the X highest-quality submissions per condition ranked by click attractiveness. Only the All Submissions row is extracted.

not_extracted.what: Open versus Blind contrasts in both experiments
not_extracted.reason: Neither arm provides generative-AI assistance. This includes quality, originality, alignment, feature prevalence, and participation comparisons wherever printed. Relevant locations include Tables 1, 2, E.2, E.3, WA-C.3/WA-C.4, and WA-D.4/WA-D.5, plus Figures 6-8, 11, and C.1.

not_extracted.what: Refinement study: originality and quality of high-quality Variation submissions versus professionally refined AI logos
not_extracted.reason: The paper recruits a separate set of professionals to polish existing AI images; it does not report random assignment of people between refinement and the contest task. The comparison also selects the high-quality contest submissions. Excluded as a non-random comparison, not an additional randomized AI configuration. PDF p. 28 (printed p. 27), Section 4.5 and Figure 10; PDF pp. 39-40 (printed pp. 38-39), Appendix D and Figures D.1-D.2.

not_extracted.what: Appendix E.1: explanatory regressions and R-squared increments relating design features to logo quality
not_extracted.reason: These regressions relate output features to output quality rather than estimating randomized AI-versus-comparison contrasts. Table E.1 is not an arm effect. PDF pp. 40-41 (printed pp. 39-40), Appendix E.1 and Table E.1.

not_extracted.what: Table E.2: Quality Cor. column and feature-selection regressions
not_extracted.reason: Quality correlations and Lasso/follow-up OLS relationships between visual features and quality are associational mechanism analyses, not effects of randomized AI assignment. PDF pp. 42-43 (printed pp. 41-42), Appendix E.2 and Table E.2. The unadjusted Submissions arm summaries are extracted separately as other output attributes.

not_extracted.what: Appendix E.2: correlation of alignment score with submission quality
not_extracted.reason: This is a correlation between two measured output attributes, not a randomized-arm contrast. PDF p. 42 (printed p. 41), Appendix E.2. The unadjusted full-sample alignment arm summaries are extracted separately.

not_extracted.what: Appendix C: correlations among style, color, and composition ratings
not_extracted.reason: These characterize the measurement dimensions rather than AI-assistance effects. PDF p. 38 (printed p. 37), Appendix C.

not_extracted.what: Designer characteristics, registration/participation rates, entry timing, and days of engagement in both experiments
not_extracted.reason: Baseline reputation, past-project quality, professionalism, hiring/review histories and hourly rates are not outcomes scored on experimental creative output; registration, entry timing and days of engagement are process measures. See PDF pp. 20-21, 29, 36-37, and 65-66 (printed pp. 19-20, 28, 35-36, and WA-21 to WA-22), Tables 1, 2, B.1, and WA-D.1. Designer counts are retained as sample information. Study 1 submission depth is retained as fluency; the unreported Study 2 submission-depth contrasts are listed separately in not_extracted.

not_extracted.what: Professional-designer focus groups and interviews about machine-generated logos
not_extracted.reason: Qualitative model-development input; no randomized assignment of participants to AI assistance with scored creative outputs. PDF pp. 10 and 12 (printed pp. 9 and 11), Section 3.

not_extracted.what: Optimization LoRA training survey and ratings of historical logo pairs
not_extracted.reason: People evaluate existing logos to train the model; they are not randomly assigned to create outputs with AI assistance. PDF pp. 14-16 (printed pp. 13-15), Section 3.2.2 and Figure 3.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix A: custom pipeline versus off-the-shelf model visual distinctiveness
not_extracted.reason: Model-only comparison on generated images, not randomized assistance to human creators. PDF pp. 46-47 (printed WA-2 to WA-3), including the paired CLIP-distance test and Figures WA-A.1/WA-A.2.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.3, validation Study 1: exemplar-variation versus exemplar-exemplar alignment
not_extracted.reason: Compares researcher-generated AI images and historical exemplars, with no randomized human-assistance arms. All individual alignment measures and composite indices in Table WA-B.3 are excluded. PDF pp. 51-55 (printed WA-7 to WA-11), Figures WA-B.2 and Table WA-B.3. The appendix study numbering is not the numbering of the two field experiments.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.3, validation Study 1: perceived resemblance of AI variations versus retrieved historical logos
not_extracted.reason: Human ratings of existing AI-made/historical work, not creative outputs produced by randomized AI-assisted participants. PDF p. 56 (printed WA-12), Figure WA-B.3.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.3, validation Study 2: visual dispersion of AI variations versus original exemplars
not_extracted.reason: The embeddings and centroid-distance comparison describe supplied AI-generated stimuli and original exemplars. They are not an across_people outcome of the randomized designers. PDF pp. 56-57 (printed WA-12 to WA-13), Figure WA-B.4 and paired dispersion test.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.3, validation Study 3: brightness and symmetry changes with Optimization LoRA
not_extracted.reason: Compares model-generated outputs with and without a fine-tuning component, with no human creators randomized to assistance. PDF pp. 58-59 (printed WA-14 to WA-15), Figure WA-B.5.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.3, validation Study 3: click-attractiveness choices with Optimization LoRA
not_extracted.reason: Raters choose between already generated images; no participants create an output with randomized AI help. PDF p. 59 (printed WA-15).

not_extracted.what: Table WA-B.4: visual-feature differences between well-performing and ill-performing logos
not_extracted.reason: The performance-defined logo groups are not randomized human AI-assistance arms. All reported feature differences and SEs in the table are excluded. PDF p. 58 (printed WA-14), Table WA-B.4; training-data context on PDF p. 15 (printed p. 14), Section 3.2.2.

not_extracted.what: Web Appendix B.4: description length and similarity to exemplars
not_extracted.reason: Model-only prompt-length comparison, without randomized human creators. PDF pp. 59-60 (printed WA-15 to WA-16), Figure WA-B.6. Figure-only statistics are not digitized.

not_extracted.what: Table E.2: Original and Variation exemplar columns
not_extracted.reason: Gallery stimuli rather than outputs produced by experimental designers. Submissions columns are extracted separately. PDF p. 43 (printed p. 42).

open_items: All printed quality and originality treatment regressions control for post-assignment submission date. Full-sample unadjusted or baseline-only-adjusted results are needed under extraction-spec rule 5. This extraction intentionally differs from the screening inventory of adjusted results.
Confirm which AI arm or arms form Variation in Appendix E and provide analytic participant and submission counts for Tables E.2-E.3. No pooled-arm membership or count is inferred.

The alignment SDs are across logos, not designer means. No participant-level SD or contrast SE is printed for unadjusted alignment or feature outcomes; repeated submissions cannot be treated as independent people.
Submission depth lacks arm means, SDs, and numerical tests. The replication does not print a fluency-specific comparison. Output totals have not been divided by participant counts.
Only submitters enter the reported outcome analyses. No intention-to-treat results including registered non-submitters are printed.

Possible designer overlap between the two contests is unstated. The screening sample_overlap identifies no other paper sharing participants, so shared_sample is null; no independent combined sample total is assigned.
The replication states that it follows the main design but does not separately restate assignment timing. Registered-by-condition counts are coded as randomized consistently with that statement.
Distinct participant counts in the high-quality originality subsets and sample membership for perception-based originality are unstated. Submission counts must not be used as people counts.

Study 1 tables print only three condition coefficients while observation totals cover the output volume associated with four arms. Fitted treatment coding and omitted Variation(4) coefficients are unclear; post-treatment adjustment independently excludes these regressions.
Final quality-rater counts and protocol are not explicitly separated from the feedback survey. Designers' countries and disclosure of the AI origin of gallery images are not stated.

The screening form flags a possible discrepancy between Figure 11B p-values and Table WA-D.5 coefficient/SE pairs. These adjusted effects are excluded here under rule 5, so no figure p-value is attached to an extracted estimate.
